headline: A low-volume relief rally left NVDA behind: desks see clean positioning but little conviction, money rotating to hyperscalers, AMD and networking, and the scandal turning into a governance and export-control story.
market_read: The 9 Nov bounce (SPX +2.3%, SOX +6.9%) was broad but thin: JPM's desk (9 Nov) reports year-to-date low high-touch volumes with a lot of the demand short covering, UBS's desk saw semis skewed for sale into strength, and JPM's Euro specialist (10 Nov) says investors want a steadier tape before re-risking, even as UBS, Vanda and JPM flow data show systematic and hedge-fund positioning washed out. NVDA decoupled, underperforming SOX by 11% (GS, 10 Nov) as the story moved from the affair to governance and export controls (Stratechery, The Information via GS, 10 Nov) and BofA took NVDA, MU and LRCX off its US 1 list; desks still relay that most investors expect it to blow over. The rotation is toward hyperscalers (UBS prime book +2.3 std long buying; GS and JPM, 10 Nov), AMD as the NVDA alternative, and networking/optical (UBS desk better to buy ANET and COHR). Infineon went from funding short to constructive after its FY27 guide (JPM, 10 Nov); CRWV reports tonight with sentiment described as overly bearish (UBS).

up.why: A funding short that just cleared its event. JPM's Silver (9 Nov) found few aggressively long and some using Infineon as a funding short; after the FY27 guide (about EUR 20bn revenue, close to EUR 4bn AI) feedback on 10 Nov was 'overwhelmingly constructive' and the stock rose 5.5%. Jefferies' Beavington (10 Nov) thinks the guide is fully in backlog and conservative. This reverses the faded-conviction read JPM gave on 23 Oct. No Bloomberg-X or HOT/BULL analog for IFX in monitor.json, so this rests on desk evidence only. 1-5 days: short covering and investors who waited for the guide can step in. 2-4 weeks: depends on semis holding the bounce and on the MATCH Act / export-control headlines staying away from European semis.
up.confirm: IFX holds the post-print gain while SOX consolidates; desks report long-only buying rather than only covering.
up.weaken: The stock gives back the move within days (a 'travel and arrive' fade), or the wider semis bounce fails.

up.why: UBS's high-touch desk (Ruple, 9 Nov) was better to buy in ANET, VIAV and COHR against some short supply while compute was for sale. Monitor: Bloomberg X attention is the second-largest riser in the universe (dz +2.28, 7-day average 124 vs 28-day 25) with the biggest tone gain (+0.37) and the stock +14% over 7 days. Caution from ANET's own history: HOT 78.6 sits in the 60-<80 band, where the 5-session median was -3.7% with 33% up (n=9, thin); BULL 81.4 has a single analog. 1-5 days: attention and flow are with it, but the name's own hot-band history argues against chasing. 2-4 weeks: Bernstein (9 Nov) sees no sector catalyst until hyperscaler capex guides in late January.
up.confirm: Desks keep reporting net buying in networking/optical on down days for compute; X tone stays positive as volume normalises.
up.weaken: The short supply UBS mentions grows, or CSCO's print (12 Nov) resets networking expectations.

up.why: Fourth straight day of the hyperscaler-over-picks-and-shovels read, now with flow data: UBS's prime book (Dwyer, 10 Nov) shows hedge funds long-buying hyperscalers (+2.3 std) on 9 Nov; GS's desk (Kamshad, 10 Nov) sees the megacaps bid pre-market while semis consolidate; JPM Market Intelligence (Tyler, 10 Nov) calls hyperscalers the tactical long. The counterpoint is Barclays' Rand (10 Nov): feedback is positive but 'everyone owns it already' and catalysts have not moved the stock. Monitor: curated-X attention is falling (dz -2.47) with the stock +5% over 7 days; HOT 38.9 (20-<40 band, own h5 median -0.03%, n=4, too thin) and BULL 46.6 (40-<60, h5 median +0.50%, 57% up, n=47). 1-5 days: the rotation persists while NVDA headlines and CRWV/NBIS prints weigh on AI compute. 2-4 weeks: Ignite investor meeting (18 Nov) is the next stock-specific test; ownership is the limit.
up.confirm: Hyperscalers keep outperforming SOX through the neocloud prints; prime-book buying continues beyond one day.
up.weaken: A broad AI-beta chase pulls money back to semis, or MSFT again fails to respond to good news, as Barclays flags.

up.why: The first 'who benefits' trade from NVDA's scandal. UBS's Ruple (10 Nov) reads 9 Nov as a rotation from NVDA into AMD (+13%) and relays a Commercial Times report of rivals seizing NVDA order cuts; Jefferies' Wong (9 Nov) names AVGO and AMD as destinations for NVDA outflows; BofA's Arya (9 Nov) says AMD, AVGO and MRVL could gain traction. Google's TPU 8tx also pairs with a custom AMD CPU (JPM, 9 Nov). This reverses last week's ledger, when UBS and Jefferies had AMD among the names sold. Monitor: Bloomberg X attention rising (dz +1.73, 7-day average 627 vs 28-day 176) with tone +0.12 and the stock +10% over 7 days; no HOT/BULL analog for AMD in monitor.json. Arya's caveat matters: if scrutiny spreads, every US supplier selling to China gets more volatile. 1-5 days: follows NVDA headlines inversely. 2-4 weeks: fades if the NVDA probe is contained.
up.confirm: AMD keeps outperforming NVDA on scandal headlines; a second source confirms order shifts.
up.weaken: NVDA's board or Congress briefing (18 Nov) contains the issue, or new export rules hit all US AI chip vendors.

up.why: Barclays' Rand (10 Nov) puts SNOW at the top of the list in infrastructure software, the preferred place to be long, with long-only investors 2-to-1 buyers on the desk over two weeks. That is consensus rather than new: Rand already had investors long SNOW into prints on 20 Oct, and Bernstein's crowding work (28 Oct) ranked SNOW the most crowded name in its software coverage. UBS's prime book adds hedge-fund buying of US software on 9 Nov (+2.1 std). No SNOW data in monitor.json. 1-5 days: benefits if software keeps outperforming semis on rotation days. 2-4 weeks: the print is the risk for a name this widely liked.
up.confirm: Software continues to be bought on the prime books; SNOW holds relative strength into its print.
up.weaken: A sharp semis recovery reverses the software bid, or any infrastructure peer disappoints the way NOW did.

down.why: Weakening sentiment, not easing crowding: the scandal widened on 9-10 Nov (FBI 'looking into' Huang, reports that NVDA's general counsel contacted Commerce during the Megaspeed probe, White House open to new export controls per The Information via GS). GS's desk (10 Nov) has NVDA underperforming SOX by 11% on 9 Nov, its biggest one-day gap in a decade; BofA removed it from the US 1 list (10 Nov, still Buy); Rothschild lists it at 12-month relative lows; Stratechery (10 Nov) says governance is now the real risk. Divergent and worth keeping: UBS and Rothschild both say most investors expect it to blow over, MS's Moore keeps it Top Pick, the ~$135B January-quarter bogey is intact, and Bernstein notes it screens cheap. Monitor: curated-X attention rising (dz +1.48) with the stock -14% over 7 days; HOT 46.8 (40-<60 band, own h5 median -0.91%, 44% up, n=32) and BULL 45.2 (h5 median +1.83%, 57% up, n=44), so no crowding signal either way. 1-5 days: headline-driven into earnings (17 Nov) and the House briefing (18 Nov). 2-4 weeks: resolves on the board probe and export-control language.
down.confirm: More official steps (subpoenas, NDAA export language, a board statement on succession); long-only selling shows up on desks.
down.weaken: The board clears Huang or Washington signals no new restrictions; earnings refocus the debate on the $135B bogey.

down.why: Weakening sentiment with attention draining away. Barclays' Rand (10 Nov) says long interest in application software is back to early-summer lows after NOW's print and nobody is adding to NOW yet despite the pullback; Rothschild (10 Nov) lists NOW at 3-month relative lows. This extends last week's ledger (GS, UBS and BofA all negative, 3-6 Nov). Monitor: Bloomberg X attention is the largest faller in the universe (dz -3.61, 7-day average 129 vs 28-day 261) with tone slightly negative and the stock -26% over 28 days; HOT 30.8 (20-<40 band, own h5 median -1.87%, 45% up, n=11) and BULL 47.6 (h5 median +0.37%, n=38). 1-5 days: no desk reports a buyer. 2-4 weeks: Rand notes NOW still gets the best feedback among large app names, so it is where interest returns first if software rotation broadens beyond infrastructure.
down.confirm: Desk buying stays confined to infrastructure/security; NOW keeps making relative lows on software up-days.
down.weaken: Long-only buying of large-cap apps appears on desks, or a peer print restores confidence in app growth.

down.why: Weakening sponsorship rather than crowding (positioning is already light). BofA removed MU from its US 1 list and its sales pitch list (10 Nov, still Buy); MS's Shawn Kim (via Amerian, 10 Nov) warns of a 2028 air pocket as memory capacity arrives in late 2027-2028; UBS's prime book had memory sold (-1.0 std) on 6 Nov; Barclays (9 Nov) already had investors long HDD / short memory. Divergent: MS's Moore ranks MU/SNDK second only to GPU/XPU, UBS's APAC strategist still likes memory, and MU rose 6% on 9 Nov. Monitor: curated-X attention rising (dz +1.14) with the stock -14% over 7 days; HOT 49.2 and BULL 42.6 (both 40-<60), where MU's own history is constructive (BULL-band h5 median +4.7%, 62% up, n=26; h10 +8.3%), which argues against pressing. 1-5 days: trades with the semis bounce. 2-4 weeks: the 2028 supply debate is the overhang.
down.confirm: More houses trim memory from focus lists; DRAM contract commentary softens at the BofA/Nanya and TrendForce calls this week.
down.weaken: Spot and contract pricing hold and long-only buyers return to memory at 2-3x forward earnings.

down.why: A new policy overhang, thinly sourced. JPM's Silver (9-10 Nov) says investors ask whether the Huang scandal revives the US MATCH Act, a headwind for ASML and ASMI that most had dismissed; GS's desk (10 Nov) relays The Information that Commerce staff are pushing rules on lithography tooling. BofA also took LRCX off its US 1 list (10 Nov), and UBS saw long-only profit taking in KLAC and AMAT (9 Nov). Against that, the ledger through 8 Nov was positive on ASML (BofA, Jefferies, JPM on valuation). Monitor: curated-X attention rising (dz +1.01) with the stock -2% over 7 days; no HOT/BULL analog for ASML. 1-5 days: sensitive to any export-control headline. 2-4 weeks: NDAA language decides whether this is real.
down.confirm: MATCH Act or lithography-tooling language appears in NDAA drafts; desks report semicap selling by long-onlys.
down.weaken: Export-control talk stays focused on AI chips and remote access, not tools.

themes.title: Positioning is clean, conviction is not
themes.text: Desks agree on the flush and disagree on the bounce. UBS (Cheong, 9-10 Nov) has risk-control exposure at 55% and CTAs net short (-5%), calling the downside feedback loop removed; Vanda (9 Nov, via Rodrigo Nascimento) has aggregate positioning at -0.93 SD, the lowest since May 2025, but notes most similar unwinds retested the low first. Against that, JPM's Creager (9 Nov) says high-touch volumes hit year-to-date lows on the +2.3% day, JPM's Heavey says a lot of the demand was short covering, UBS's desk saw semis skewed for sale into strength with long-only engagement, and JPM's Silver (10 Nov) describes investors 'peeking out of the bunkers'. MS's QDS still expects $30-40B of systematic selling this week. Wells Fargo's strategist (Kwon, 10 Nov) moved AI infrastructure to neutral, saying a deceleration is priced but an EPS downturn is not.

themes.title: The 2028 air pocket is the fundamental disagreement
themes.text: MS is arguing with itself in public: Wilson and Moore say the correction is near its end and '2028' is the usual months-13-to-24 worry, while Shawn Kim says memory and the supply chain add capacity into late 2027-2028 just as MS's own model now has US data-center additions flat in 2028 (5 GW pushed to 2029). UBS's Arcuri (9 Nov) thinks SOX already implies about a 35% cut to CY28 EPS; MS's McVeigh sees only ~12 GW of Texas/Ohio pipeline at risk through 2030. GW figures here are each broker's own basis and are not comparable across notes.

themes.title: NVDA: governance replaces 'affair' as the frame
themes.text: Stratechery (Thompson, 10 Nov, independent author, forwarded by Daniel Grozdea) ranks Monday's reports by how they play in Washington: the general counsel's contact with Commerce during the Megaspeed probe and an under-count of chips sold matter more than the relationship itself. Sell-side and desks are mostly on the other side: BofA's Arya 'not yet an earnings event', MS's Moore Top Pick, UBS and Rothschild relaying that investors expect it to blow over. The gap between the independent read and the desk consensus is the thing to watch into 17-18 Nov.

themes.title: Software: infrastructure and security bought, apps ignored
themes.text: Barclays' Rand (10 Nov) sees no broad rotation back to software despite the semis volatility: long-onlys buy infrastructure, security and vertical SaaS (SNOW, NET, PANW, CRWD; hedge funds prefer OKTA), with no buying in apps after NOW. UBS's prime book did show hedge-fund buying of US software on 9 Nov (+2.1 std). Bernstein's Seidman is more cautious on cyber sentiment because of funding-flow events.
